Senses.Explanation: The one in charge is a personified title used in Chan self-address, questions, equations, and corrections. Ruiyan Shiyan calls out to the title each day, answers himself, and tells himself to stay alert; Yunfeng repeats that case and criticizes it as activity in a ghost cave. Dongshan Liangjie asks which one is an interlocutor's one in charge, rejects the answer that it is the person presently responding, and presses the distinction between guest and host. Tianru Weize explicitly says that mind, on each person's own share, is called oneself and is also called the one in charge. Zhongfeng Mingben groups Ruiyan's title with Linji Yixuan's true person of no rank, while Yulin Tongxiu warns against mistaking the bright, numinous identity-consciousness for realization of it. Zhaozhou Congshen says that after seeing him it is no other person, only the one in charge, and warns against seeking it outside. The record thereby bends an ordinary household title into something publicly called, located, equated, and tested.
Senses.Note: The exact headword has 738 hits in 198 allowlisted texts. Seven independent witnesses satisfy the frequency floor. Self-calling, direct questions, equations, and corrective uses concern the same personified title, not different referents, so they remain one sense.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In his Extensive Record (天目中峰廣錄), Zhongfeng Mingben says that many people take Ruiyan's one in charge together with Linji Yixuan's true person of no rank.
